newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end touch lower, well supported.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end touch lower, well supported.

text.p: French shares ended with modest losses, after a round of profit-taking, traders said. The market had been looking to consolidate after recent strong rises.
However, as Wall Street continues to climb, Paris is well supported and brokers are eyeing 2,300 on the CAC index in the coming weeks. A buy programme was lifting the Dow in the Paris late afternoon.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 2.06 points or 0.09 percent at 2,275.08, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down three at 2,274 from Monday's close.
Volume was a hefty 5.66 billion francs.
* Jitters on the franc helped trigger profit-taking. Brokers said the continuing truck drivers' strike raised concerns, as did dissenting views on France's strong franc policy.
* Index heavyweights Elf and Total weakened respectively 0.42 percent to 454.50 francs and 0.33 percent to 424.10, due to falls in world crude prices, as Iraqi oil looks set to enter the market.

* Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk told a key parliamentary deputy he would consider making a new offer for Thomson if Lagardere missed the end-year deadline, according to finance committee minutes.
* Alcatel ended down 1.7 percent at 462.10 francs, while Lagardere closed down 1.21 percent at 155.
* UAP said after the close its maximum residual insurance risk to Eurotunnel was 75 million francs and it was impossible to quantify damage caused by last week's fire.
Eurotunnel closed down 7.86 percent at 6.45 francs. The company is holding a news conference on Wednesday at 0800 GMT.
* Carrefour pleases, up 2.81 percent at 3,180. The retailer is viewed as true blue chip in foreign portfolios.
* Canal Plus firmed 1.44 percent to 1,198, making up some of recent losses following a bearish valuation study.
* Thomson-CSF climbs 0.92 percent to 165 francs. The company has won Swiss and Polish military radio contracts.
* Sanofi trims gains to end up 1.5 percent at 455.70 francs. The stock has firmed more than 40 percent this year, boosted by merger speculation with Rhone-Poulenc .
* Cie de Suez firms 1.8 percent to 225. Suez and Paribas, up 0.3 percent at 363.20, are seen as potential candidates for consolidation, following the Axa -UAP merger.
* Bouygues dips 0.19 percent to 534 on profit-taking.
* Resistance seen on the CAC at 2,294/96, then 2,303/05, and support at 2,268/70 and 2,257/59.
